destination.name: Port Lincoln
destination.tagline: Seafood capital on Boston Bay, with shark cage diving and wild coast
destination.description: Port Lincoln sits on Boston Bay at the southern tip of the Eyre Peninsula and is known as Australia's seafood capital. Tuna and other seafood come off the working harbour, and boats leave from here for great white shark cage diving. Lookouts, a murals trail and a maritime museum fill a day in town, and Lincoln National Park and Whalers Way lie a short drive south.

goodToKnow.title: Whalers Way needs a permit
goodToKnow.detail: Whalers Way is private land. Buy a permit before you enter, from the visitor centre or online, and expect unsealed roads.

goodToKnow.title: Book shark dives ahead
goodToKnow.detail: Cage diving trips leave from the town harbour and sell out in peak season, so book before you arrive.

goodToKnow.title: Distances are long
goodToKnow.detail: Adelaide is about 650 km away, so plan a fly-in or an overnight stop on the drive.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring mild weather for coastal walks and drives, while summer is hot and busy.
